_note: Batch 2 draft (author pass, pre-review). 4 sci-fi theme tag sets completing the sample set of 10 (#0 original + 5 batch1 + 4 here). Requirements: sci-fi, artifacts, alien civilizations (need NOT be fallen). Resource tie-ins welcome, not mandatory. Psychic OPTIONAL (per Sam) — kept light here for breadth. Deliberately covers gaps round-1 flagged: an 'absent' alien status, a crowded LIVING galaxy, and tones (awe, outbreak-thriller, mercantile-noir, stewardship) not present in batch 1.

sets.title: The Inheritance
sets.hook: Humanity arrives inside a working megastructure the size of a solar system — and its builders are simply GONE, no bodies, no war, no graves. The artifacts are control-keys that switch pieces of it on; the resource is the structure's stored energy and matter; the mystery is not how they died but where they went, and what the structure was built to DO.
sets.artifact_flavor: Control-keys and access-sigils that activate dormant megastructure systems; each hunted key lights up a new region and a new clue to the builders' purpose — and risks waking a system that was off for a reason.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Scale and AWE, not bodies. Aliens left no corpses to excavate and no live presence to negotiate with — only an inhabited machine and an unanswered 'why'. Exploitation is of the structure itself.

sets.title: The Quarantine Worlds
sets.hook: An alien civilization didn't fall to greed — it was consumed by a self-replicating extinction-vector (gray-goo / memetic / biological) it failed to contain. The artifacts are quarantined relics and scattered cure-fragments; hunting them is a race to assemble containment before the colony becomes the next carrier — every relic you crack could be the cure or the next outbreak.
sets.artifact_flavor: Sealed quarantine-relics and cure-fragments; assembling the right set yields containment, but each is a live hazard — opening the wrong one reseeds the plague in the present.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Outbreak-thriller tension and an EXTERNAL killer the aliens were victims of (not perpetrators of their own fall, unlike #0). The hunt has an active downside: you can lose by spreading what you sought.

sets.title: The Long Bazaar
sets.hook: The galaxy is ALIVE and crowded — dozens of minor alien species trading, scheming, and feuding in a busy frontier. Artifacts are black-market curios whose value is their provenance (and half are forgeries); the resource is a contested commodity everyone wants a cut of. The story is who you deal with, who you cross, and which relic's history is even real.
sets.artifact_flavor: Curios and relics traded on a black market; an artifact's power is inseparable from its (often forged) provenance chain — hunting one means tracing or faking its history through living factions.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: A LIVED-IN, crowded, mercantile galaxy of many small living species — not a grand empire, tomb, or single organism. Tone is noir/political; the 'civilization' is a marketplace, and the hunt is social, not archaeological.

sets.title: The Gardeners' Patience
sets.hook: The world is being deliberately cultivated — life here is too convenient, too aimed — by gardeners who are present but never seen. The artifacts are their shaping-tools, left in the soil to steer evolution; the resource is the engineered biosphere itself. The mystery: is the colony a welcome guest, a pest, or the next thing being cultivated?
sets.artifact_flavor: Gardeners' shaping-tools — terraforming seeds, gene-looms, soil-shrines — that let you steer or exploit the living world, while possibly tripping the gardeners' attention; each reveals a little of their method and intent.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Aliens are HIDDEN and active (neither dead nor openly present), and the theme is stewardship-vs-exploitation with the player possibly being the experiment — a moral/ecological frame absent from the others.
